title: gcloud: configurations, contexts and more than one account

videos.script: Every setting gcloud has is a property. Project, region, account. A configuration is a named set of them. {{properties}} Your lab has used one configuration since lesson 1, and that is why no command has needed to name the project. {{default}} Now a second one, for production. It starts empty, with nothing but what you give it. {{prod}} When a property is set in more than one place, the most specific wins. A flag, then an environment variable, then the configuration. {{precedence}} The planner never makes production the active configuration. A terminal that works on production says so in a variable. {{habit}} Credentials are stored apart from configurations. And production runs as a service account, impersonated, set once as a property. {{impersonation}} Google refuses the lab's placeholder, at the service that issues the token. {{refusal}} Then format and filter: the two flags that turn gcloud from something a person reads into something a script can trust. {{end}}
